title: Wall Street Tried to Stop Hyperliquid. Now It's Buying In 🤯
alt_hooks: Hyperliquid's HYPE jumped 17% after the NYSE owner made its move.
Did the New York Stock Exchange just adopt Hyperliquid?
Stanley Druckenmiller and the NYSE owner just backed Hyperliquid.

scenes.line: Wall Street tried to stop it. Now it is buying in.
This spring, the owner of the New York Stock Exchange pushed regulators to rein in Hyperliquid.
Two weeks later, its own CEO called the eleven-person exchange bigger than Nasdaq.
Then on October 29, ICE bought a stake in Trade XYZ, a market built on Hyperliquid.

receipt.headline: HYPE teases all-time high as NYSE owner ICE eyes US Hyperliquid perps

scenes.line: The plan? Hyperliquid-style perpetual futures for American retail traders.
Trade XYZ says its markets did over $650 billion in volume in just over a year.
And the HYPE token? It jumped 17% on the news.

receipt.headline: Hyperliquid (HYPE) Price: NYSE Owner Picks Its Network and the Token Jumps 17%

scenes.line: It still needs regulators to say yes. The same regulators ICE called on this spring.

lesson: When a coin jumps on a headline, read the whole story before you act.
description: In spring 2026, ICE, the owner of the New York Stock Exchange, and CME reportedly pushed US regulators to rein in Hyperliquid. Two weeks later ICE's CEO called the 11-person exchange "bigger than Nasdaq." On October 29, 2026, ICE took a minority stake in Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to US retail traders, pending regulatory approval. HYPE jumped about 17% on the news.
pinned: Wall Street joining crypto: good news or bad news for traders?
